questions: What is the exact mathematical definition of B^p - is it matrix exponentiation or element-wise exponentiation?
How should the sum of all possible matrices B^p be computed - should we sum the matrices first then take the p-th power, or take the p-th power of each matrix then sum?
What is the order of operations for computing the sum - do we compute B^p for each of the (p-1)^K matrices first, then sum all results?
How should we handle the case when p=1, given that the constraint says p is prime but also allows p≤10^9?
What is the expected output format when N=1 and there are no rows to print?
Should the final result matrix elements be reduced modulo p before output, or is the sum already guaranteed to be within the correct range?
How should we interpret "each element of the sum" - does this mean we output the entire resulting matrix or just specific elements?
What is the precise definition of matrix multiplication being used - standard matrix multiplication over what field/ring?
answers: B^p is standard matrix exponentiation: repeated matrix multiplication.
Compute B^p for each possible matrix B, then sum the results; do not sum first then exponentiate.
Yes. Compute B^p for each of the (p-1)^K possible matrices, then sum all resulting matrices element-wise.
p = 1 is not prime, so it is excluded from the constraints.
With N=1, there is one row containing one element; print that element.
Yes. Each element of the resulting matrix should be reduced modulo p individually before output.
Output the entire resulting matrix, with each row on a separate line and elements space-separated.
Standard matrix multiplication, with all arithmetic performed modulo p.
inline_prompts: You are given a prime number p and an N \times N matrix A = (A_{i,j}) (1\leq i,j\leq N). Each element of A is an integer between 0 and p-1, inclusive. Consider a matrix B obtained by replacing each zero in A with an integer between 1 and p-1, inclusive. There are (p-1)^K such matrices B, where K is the number of zeros in A. Find each element, modulo p, of the sum of B^p. B^p is standard matrix exponentiation: repeated matrix multiplication. Input The input is given from Standard Input in the following format: N p A_{1,1} \cdots A_{1,N} \vdots A_{N,1} \cdots A_{N,N} Output Print N lines. Constraints - 1 \leq N \leq 100 - p is a prime such that 1 \leq p \leq 10^9. - 0 \leq A_{i,j} \leq p-1 - All input values are integers.
